title: Typed class, interface, trait and enum constants
summary: PHP 8.3 lets constants declared on classes, interfaces, traits and enums carry an explicit type, checked at declaration and for covariance on override.
new_code_policy: When the project's feature ceiling is PHP 8.3 or newer, declare an explicit type on every new class, interface, trait or enum constant instead of leaving it untyped.
existing_code_policy: Do not bulk-retrofit types onto constants that predate this rule's ceiling; add a type only when a constant is already being touched for another reason, since each addition needs its own check that overriding declarations in subclasses or implementors stay covariant.
guideline: Prefer typed class, interface, trait and enum constants once the feature ceiling reaches PHP 8.3; leave already-shipped untyped constants alone unless you are revising them anyway.
details: PHP 8.3 (RFC typed_class_constants) added optional type declarations to constants declared in classes, interfaces, traits and enums. The engine enforces the declared type at the point of declaration and requires an overriding declaration in a subclass or implementing class to use a covariant type. This is purely additive: untyped constants remain valid PHP, and giving a new constant a type changes no runtime behavior for code that does not declare or override it. A separate PHP 8.4 change made a number of built-in extension classes' own constants typed; that is extensions adopting this language feature for their internal constants, not a further change to the feature itself (see notes).
notes: PHP 8.4 made a number of built-in extension classes' own constants typed, applying this language feature to internal classes; that is extensions adopting the feature, not a further extension of typed class constants itself.
